demo.title: Switch the brand. The code stays put.
demo.lead: Pick Aurum, Nova, Fiesta or Ultra, then flip light and dark. Colors, fonts, radii and spacing change. The components underneath don't.

architecture.title: Six layers. Only one of them is the brand.
architecture.lead: A component never knows which brand it is in. It asks for a meaning, the theme picks a step on a color ramp, and only the brand file holds real colors, fonts and radii. Every number below is counted from the demo's tokens at build time.

components.name: Components
components.detail: Buttons, cards and chips read meanings, never raw values.

theme.name: Theme
theme.detail: Semantic colors: text, fill, border. Light and dark are an axis of their own.

typography.name: Typography
typography.detail: Built from the brand's fonts and the core type scale.

map.name: Map
map.detail: Tints and shades calculated from brand colors, so nobody picks them by hand.

brand.name: Brand
brand.detail: The only file that changes when you add a brand.

core.name: Core
core.detail: The raw scale: sizes, radii, weights, base colors.

explorer.title: Follow one token through the layers
explorer.themeNote: Switch the site theme at the top right: light and dark take different steps of the same ramp.

notes.base: step 500 is the brand color itself

how.title: How a brand gets from Figma to production

steps.title: Figma
steps.detail: Figma Variables and Token Studio hold the same layers: primitives, meanings, components. A designer edits a value and never a component.

steps.title: Sync
steps.detail: Token Studio pushes JSON to Git. A build turns it into CSS custom properties and checks keys, layer references and contrast before anything ships.

steps.title: Ship
steps.detail: The product switches brand and theme with two attributes on the root element. Same markup, same components, one release for every brand.

sections.limits: What the system does not solve

tokenLayers.title: Three layers of tokens
tokenLayers.lead: A component asks for a meaning. A meaning points to a primitive. Only primitives hold raw values, so nothing above them ever hardcodes a color.

layers.name: Component
layers.detail: Reads a meaning. Never a raw value.

layers.name: Semantic
layers.detail: Says what a value is for: text, fill, border.

layers.name: Primitive
layers.detail: The only layer with real colors, sizes and fonts.

twoAxes.title: Two axes: brand and mode
twoAxes.lead: Brand and light/dark are independent. Four brands times two modes give eight combinations from the same components. Pick a cell to see that lobby.
twoAxes.gridLabel: Pick a brand and a mode

components.title: Components
components.lead: Component sets in Figma and the properties each one exposes. The same component appears in every brand.

pipeline.title: Pipeline
pipeline.lead: From a design decision to a CSS variable in production, with checks on the way.

nodes.name: Build
nodes.detail: Token JSON to CSS custom properties, with checks.

nodes.name: CSS
nodes.detail: One file of variables per brand and theme.

codeProof.title: Proof in code
codeProof.lead: Open DevTools on the demo: the brand is an attribute on the root element, and the computed values follow it.
codeProof.first: Pick another brand to see what changes.
codeProof.noData: Token data is not available in this build.

limits.title: What the system does not solve
limits.lead: A token system makes brands cheap to add. It does not make every brand decision for you.

items.title: Content
items.detail: Copy, tone of voice and imagery stay with each brand.

items.title: Illustration
items.detail: Tokens carry colors and sizes. Custom artwork is separate work.

items.title: Motion
items.detail: Durations and easings can be tokens, but motion design is its own discipline.

items.title: Legal requirements of markets
items.detail: Age notices, licences and responsible-gaming text differ per market and need their own review.
